source_audit.correction: The supplied draft attributes Model or Harness? to Taraghi. The inspected paper is by Raj and colleagues. Taraghi and colleagues wrote the separate MCP-software-fault study.
Dependency on a nonsurviving effect is distinct from merely discarding a speculative branch. Both are represented, without pretending the two labels are identical.

An outbox can atomically persist a local business change and local event intent. Its relay can still redeliver, and it does not add outcome visibility or atomic participation to an opaque external provider.

A key may be randomly generated once and durably retained. Deterministic content-only derivation is not required and can collapse two legitimate identical requests. Scope, payload binding, retention and atomic target handling matter.

A current absence read, even if fresh, does not prove a previously queued request cannot execute later. Safe retry needs the relevant target-side guarantee or positively established termination of the earlier attempt.

A saga is a deliberate compensation model, not simply a broken two-phase commit. Compensation may restore a valid business state without restoring the exact old state, and must account for intervening legitimate changes.

Unconditional undo under an unknown outcome is unsafe. A target-supported conditional compensation primitive can legitimately resolve that condition atomically even if the caller does not first know the outcome.
A gateway can reject future stale admissions; it cannot retract an already forwarded, uncontrollable remote command. The enforcement point and in-flight set must be named.
Missing heartbeat means suspected failure, not proof of death. A live heartbeat also does not prove mission progress.

Neither a second LLM nor a deterministic checker is automatically an independent truth oracle. Verification needs appropriate evidence, a valid predicate and protection from common-mode or subject-controlled failure.

A signature or hash can establish origin/integrity within a trust model, not the truth, completeness, freshness or physical meaning of the signed assertion. Provider signatures are not universally required when other trustworthy observation paths suffice.
A sandbox label, data tag or signed tool description is not a universal injection or containment guarantee. Actual capabilities, mounts, egress and trusted enforcement still matter.

Error handling must use the actual provider contract. A timeout or some server error responses may follow an applied effect; some authentication failures are legitimately refreshable. Blanket retry/fatal classifications are not sound.

Durable lineage does not require retaining every private reasoning token forever. It requires sufficient scoped intent, decisions, constraints, effects, evidence, corrections and continuation records under an explicit retention policy.

Not every task can enumerate all future work up front. Snapshot, watermark, pagination or another justified dynamic closure rule may be needed. A success count alone does not prove correct set membership.
Ask the Tool, Do Not Guess supports tool-progress and serving-resource analysis. It does not establish the cross-tenant corruption or prefix-splicing incidents asserted in the supplied draft.
The cited context-drift study explicitly says its software-domain follow-up did not replicate the travel-domain broadcast degradation. The number is not a universal property of agent communication.
DOM-hidden text, tiny rendered text and pixels absent from a raster are different channels. A screenshot model cannot read text that is genuinely absent from its pixel input.

The retrieved specification page uses /.well-known/agent-card.json. The older agent.json path in the supplied draft should not be presented as the checked current path. Discovery metadata is not an authority grant.
The v1 Table 8 caption states 21 Level-3 categories, but the inspected PDF table shows 20 named rows. This catalog maps the visible rows and does not manufacture a twenty-first.
Characterizing Faults in Agentic AI contains an inconsistent 2018 journal-template footer. It is cited here as the retrieved arXiv preprint, not as a verified 2018 journal publication.
The retrieved SOSP item is the authors' slide deck. It is not silently represented as a full-text proceedings-paper review.

sources.title: Trofimov & Novikov, When Tool Calls Succeed but Workflows Fail (2609.15397v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: External-effect history, A1-A8 and interface-dependent guarantee boundaries. Not a proof that a particular deployed harness implements the prerequisites.

sources.title: Raj et al., Model or Harness? (2607.28802v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: Interaction-centric, role-specific fault classification. Illustrative reports are not a population prevalence estimate. This is not the Taraghi paper.

sources.title: Taraghi, Morovati & Khomh, Real Faults in MCP Software (2603.05637v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: MCP-specific software defects, including setup, discovery, connections, tools, host integration and diagnostics. Counts describe the sampled issue corpus.

sources.title: Shah et al., Characterizing Faults in Agentic AI (2603.06847v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: Agent software fault types, symptoms and causes are separate taxonomies. PDF contains template publication metadata; cited as an arXiv preprint, not as the journal implied by that footer.

sources.title: Cemri et al., Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (2503.13657v3)
sources.scope_and_limit: Fourteen coordination failure labels. Multi-agent evidence informs boundary analysis; it does not imply Camden should introduce multiple reasoning executors.

sources.title: Kokane et al., ToolScan (2411.13547v2)
sources.scope_and_limit: Tool-call error classes, including missing/repeated calls, argument name/type/value, function identity and formatting. These are not all external-effect failures.

sources.title: Beyond Function Calling: ToolBench-X (2606.25819v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: Five tool-environment hazard families in controlled, recoverable fixtures; do not generalize fixture recoverability to arbitrary providers.

sources.title: Zhang et al., When Agentic Executions Fail / AgentChaosBench (2608.14680v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: Ten injected runtime faults, plus no-fault controls. Injection families and trace-localization scores are not a complete incident ontology.

sources.title: Garg et al., MemFail (2605.26667v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: Separates summary, storage, retrieval and downstream reasoning failures. Includes coexistence and conditional facts; synthetic benchmark limits apply.

sources.title: Memory-Induced Tool-Drift in LLM Agents (2605.24941v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: Stored personal tendencies can affect tool parameters outside relevant scope. Effect sizes are benchmark-specific.

sources.title: Dong et al., Memory Injection Attacks via Query-Only Interaction (2503.03704v4)
sources.scope_and_limit: Query-only memory poisoning mechanism. Specific attack success rates do not apply to every memory architecture.

sources.title: Al-Tawaha et al., Remembering More, Risking More (2605.17830v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: Longitudinal safety risks in memory-equipped agents. Not evidence for every compression-laundering story in the supplied draft.

sources.title: When Errors Become Narratives (2606.14589v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: Silent failures and fluent narratives that obscure them. Case-study findings are not universal failure frequencies.

sources.title: Lilienthal & Hong, Mind the Gap (2508.17155)
sources.scope_and_limit: Check/use races in agent tool workflows. Atomic or conditional operations are still subject to the actual target contract.

sources.title: Liu et al., Ask the Tool, Do Not Guess (2609.18849v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: Tool-progress signals for serving/cache decisions. Does not establish cross-tenant KV corruption or semantic state splicing.

sources.title: El Yagoubi et al., AgentLeak (2602.11510v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: Seven disclosure channels and six attack families. Coverage and evaluation strength differ across channels; a trust-boundary violation is not automatically a public breach.

sources.title: Barke et al., AgentRx (2602.02475v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: Failure localization through constraints and execution evidence. An inferred critical step is an analysis result, not omniscient causal ground truth.

sources.title: Guo et al., AgentEval (2604.23581v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: Step/dependency-aware evaluation and hierarchical categories. DAG assumptions and judge calibration constrain applicability. Table 8 in v1 visibly enumerates 20 Level-3 rows although its caption states 21; the table was checked in the PDF image. The crosswalk uses the 20 visible rows and does not invent a twenty-first.

sources.title: Microsoft AI Red Team, Taxonomy of Failure Modes in Agentic AI Systems v2.0
sources.scope_and_limit: Thirty-four safety/security labels; prospective threats are separately marked by the document. It is not a certification checklist.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026
sources.scope_and_limit: Ten umbrella risk classes. Umbrella labels are crosswalks, not ten additional non-overlapping mechanisms. Official launch article independently enumerates ASI01-ASI10. The resource-page download click failed; no claim of full PDF retrieval is made.

sources.title: Anthropic, Effective harnesses for long-running agents
sources.scope_and_limit: Session continuation, progress artifacts and end-to-end testing. Not proof of external provider delivery or universal model independence.

sources.title: AWS Builders Library, Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
sources.scope_and_limit: Intent identity, parameter binding, atomic deduplication, late requests. Identical parameters need not mean identical intent.

sources.title: Stripe API, Idempotent requests
sources.scope_and_limit: Key retention, parameter comparison and cached outcomes for this documented API surface. Do not conflate v1 and v2 semantics.

sources.title: Stripe API v2 overview
sources.scope_and_limit: Different API version, method and scope constraints; v2 documentation describes a different deduplication interval from v1.

sources.title: AWS Prescriptive Guidance, Transactional outbox
sources.scope_and_limit: Atomic local data/outbox commit does not eliminate duplicate relay delivery or supply remote transaction participation.

sources.title: Microsoft Azure, Compensating Transaction pattern
sources.scope_and_limit: Business compensation need not restore exact initial state or follow reverse order. Compensation itself can fail and must account for concurrent changes.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18, Transaction Isolation
sources.scope_and_limit: Isolation anomalies and serializable transaction retry requirements. Database transaction guarantees do not automatically span external tools.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18, Continuous Archiving and PITR
sources.scope_and_limit: Recovery history, archive continuity and timelines. Restoring a database does not restore external effects to the same point in time.

sources.title: SQLite, How To Corrupt An SQLite Database File
sources.scope_and_limit: Durability, journals, locking, backup pairing, storage and memory faults. Historical implementation incidents are not assertions that every current version has them.

sources.title: Temporal, Workflow Definition
sources.scope_and_limit: Replay determinism and version compatibility. Workflow replay and external activity effects are different boundaries.

sources.title: Kleppmann, How to do distributed locking
sources.scope_and_limit: Lease expiry, process pauses and target-enforced fencing. A client-side lock cannot fence a target that ignores its token.

sources.title: Fischer, Lynch & Paterson, Impossibility of Distributed Consensus with One Faulty Process
sources.scope_and_limit: Termination limit under its asynchronous deterministic consensus model; not a universal statement that practical systems cannot recover.

sources.title: Lee et al., Implementing Linearizability at Large Scale and Low Latency
sources.scope_and_limit: Completion records, durable duplicate handling and record lifetime. Cited as the conference presentation, not mistaken for the full proceedings paper.

sources.title: IETF RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics
sources.scope_and_limit: Method semantics, conditionals, status codes and retries. HTTP success has the meaning supplied by the endpoint, not a universal business-completion meaning.

sources.title: IETF RFC 9700, OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice
sources.scope_and_limit: Token audience, redirect validation, authorization binding and refresh security. Possession of credentials does not supply business authorization.

sources.title: IETF RFC 8785, JSON Canonicalization Scheme
sources.scope_and_limit: Canonical bytes for signing/hashing. Does not establish truth, authorization, completeness or harmlessness of those bytes.

sources.title: IETF RFC 3339, Date and Time on the Internet
sources.scope_and_limit: Instant representation and offsets; future civil recurrences still need zone and recurrence semantics.

sources.title: Kubernetes, API Concepts
sources.scope_and_limit: Versioned reads, conditional writes, watches and pagination. Contracts must be checked for the actual server version.

sources.title: Kubernetes, Garbage Collection
sources.scope_and_limit: Owners, dependent resources and cleanup boundaries. Useful precedent for orphan and incorrectly collected work artifacts.

sources.title: Kubernetes, Controllers
sources.scope_and_limit: Desired/observed state reconciliation; declarative state alone does not prove a live controller or converged outcome.

sources.title: Google SRE Book, Handling Overload
sources.scope_and_limit: Admission, overload, queueing and load shedding. Model resources and recovery work participate in the same capacity constraints.

sources.title: Google SRE Book, Addressing Cascading Failures
sources.scope_and_limit: Retry amplification, shared dependency failures and recovery load. Independent-looking components can share a fault domain.

sources.title: MCP Security Best Practices, 2025-11-25 documentation
sources.scope_and_limit: Confused deputy, token passthrough, SSRF, sessions and scope. The protocol does not automatically enforce every host security requirement.

sources.title: A2A Protocol specification, v1.0-era page retrieved 2026-09-22
sources.scope_and_limit: Task states, identities, streams, capabilities and discovery. The retrieved page uses /.well-known/agent-card.json; signatures are optional and are not execution grants.

sources.title: GitHub Actions, Secure use reference
sources.scope_and_limit: Untrusted contributions, workflow privilege and self-hosted runner risks. Public documentation discovery is separate from executing public code.

sources.title: SLSA v1.1, Supply chain threats
sources.scope_and_limit: Threats across source, build, dependencies and artifact distribution. Provenance narrows claims; it does not certify semantic correctness.

sources.title: MITRE CWE-78, OS Command Injection
sources.scope_and_limit: Untrusted data crossing into shell syntax. Defensive mechanism classification only; catalog examples contain no operational attack payload.

sources.title: MITRE CWE-918, Server-Side Request Forgery
sources.scope_and_limit: Untrusted destinations reaching unintended services. Applies to tools, callbacks, document fetches and registries.

sources.title: MITRE CWE-400, Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
sources.scope_and_limit: Compute, memory, storage and network exhaustion. Each concrete resource boundary still needs its own measurement and enforcement.

sources.title: Lamport, Specifying Systems
sources.scope_and_limit: Specification and model-checking foundation. The existence of a model or proof does not establish implementation refinement or environment assumptions.

sources.title: Dong et al., DeltaBox (2605.22781)
sources.scope_and_limit: Checkpoint/rollback of sandbox process and file state. Does not promise rollback of externally observed or physical effects.

sources.title: Rodrigues, Hallucination as Context Drift (2606.21666v1)
sources.scope_and_limit: A broadcast-contamination result in travel scenarios did not replicate in the software domain. Not a universal numerical penalty for synchronization.

sources.title: Debenedetti et al., AgentDojo (2406.13352)
sources.scope_and_limit: Prompt-injection evaluation with tool use and utility tradeoffs. No defense in this catalog is claimed universally injection-proof.

sources.title: Verified Tool Calls Improve LLM Agent Reliability Under Non-Atomic Failures (2608.02645)
sources.scope_and_limit: Timeout, visibility, partial-operation and stale-conflict fixtures. Verification policy remains conditional on target capabilities.

sources.title: Albayaydh et al., Beyond the Leaderboard (2607.05775)
sources.scope_and_limit: Cross-benchmark grouping and measurement-validity concerns. Full text was not retrieved; no fine-grained incident claims are taken from it.

sources.title: RFC 6973, Privacy Considerations for Internet Protocols
sources.scope_and_limit: Data minimization, disclosure, correlation, secondary use and retention. Not jurisdiction-specific legal advice or a certification of compliance.

sources.title: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook, Verification and Validation Plan Outline
sources.scope_and_limit: Separates requirements verification, intended-use validation and integrated-system evidence. Used as a precedent for original boundary examples, not as an agent incident report.
